title: Yiqtol and Tenseless Forms
description: Yiqtol uses prefixes to mark person. Some related forms express possibility, desire, command, or verbal action without a fixed time reference.

blocks.html: Yiqtol has a prefix in every person and suffixes in some gender-and-number forms. It can express future, repeated, general, or modal meanings, so it is not equivalent to one English tense. Some forms are identical and must be interpreted from context. Imperatives, jussives, cohortatives, and infinitives share parts of the verbal system but have distinct clause roles.

didYouKnow: According to OSHB/MorphHB (CC BY 4.0), the most frequent word in this unit is יִקְטֹל (yiqṭōl), occurring 1 times in the Westminster Leningrad Codex.
